newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-FORECAST-NAB year net seen up slightly.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-FORECAST-NAB year net seen up slightly.

text.p: National Australia Bank Ltd (NAB) is expected to have weathered increasing domestic competition to extract a 3.8 percent rise in net profits for the year to September 30, analysts said.
Analysts pegged their average forecast for NAB's 1995/96 net profit before abnormals at A$2.01 billion, a record result up from A$1.936 billion a year ago.
Forecasts ranged from A$1.93 billion to A$2.03 billion.
NAB's results are due to be released on Thursday.
"They've made a big effort to contain costs in Australia and New Zealand. Also in Australia they've made some market share gains in lending," one analyst said.

NAB, which is Australia's largest bank in terms of market capitalisation, assets and earnings, had suffered tighter margins at the hands of new entrants, especially in the domestic home lending market, analysts said.
"They have (grown market share) in Australia and that's been a positive but the outlook is for low earnings growth in Australia," an analyst said.
Most analysts said NAB had achieved the rigorous cost control objectives it set a year ago, despite wage increases won by its staff during wage negotiations in the first quarter of calendar 1996.
"They had quite significant reductions in expenses," said one analyst, who expected, however, the bank's cost to income ratio to have fallen only slightly due to the squeeze on margins.
Analysts said the year's profit growth would be helped by the inclusion of 11 months worth of earnings from the bank's U.S. unit, Michigan National Corp.
In August, NAB managing director Don Argus said the unit was performing exceedingly well.
But not all offshore units had enjoyed a good year, analysts noted, with bad debts from the company's U.K. business seen rising significantly.
Analysts forecast NAB's bad and doubful debt charges for fical 1995/96 at an average of A$353 million, up from A$116 million a year earlier.
"Most of that bad debt expense is coming out of the U.K. operations," one analyst said.

One analyst noted a small positive for the bank would come in the form of higher other income from its trading activities around July's 50 basis point cut in official interest rates by the Reserve Bank of Australia.

"The bank was a noted winner when they had the (July) easing. It was on the right side of the fence so the other income line might look better because they've got better trading income this time around," he said.

Analysts hoped NAB would outline how it would extract improved earnings growth from the Australian and U.K. financial services markets when it announces its results around 0130 GMT (12.30 p.m.) on Thursday.
NAB reported a net profit after abnormals of A$1.97 billion in the year to September 30, 1995 from A$1.71 billion in 1993/94.
